subject: Deliver local semantic indexing
description:
## What to build

Deliver the explicit local lifecycle that provisions the approved embedding model, incrementally indexes managed Markdown into derivative local vector state, reports readiness without mutation, and leaves deterministic recall unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The approved shared model is provisioned idempotently by init.
- [ ] Indexing creates, updates, and deletes only derivative per-vault state.
- [ ] Status accurately reports vault, model, index, and recall readiness.
- [ ] Normal tests remain deterministic and offline, and bun run check passes.
- [ ] Current deterministic recall remains operational.

## Source

Derived from .specs/PLAN-agentic-memory-semantic-index.md: Outcome, Scope, Implementation Phases, and Completion Criteria.
context:
## Execution context

Coordinate the approved semantic-index implementation phases while keeping Markdown authoritative and production recall deterministic until a later recall project activates semantic retrieval.

## Relevant project context

- Core workflows and adapters belong in packages/core.
- CLI commands are thin adapters in packages/cli.
- The canonical vault template is packages/vault-template/template.
- Follow AGENTS.md architecture, Effect, type-safety, and dependency-direction requirements.
- Do not restructure the independent retrieval benchmark merely to inspect index internals.

## Dependency context

None at the epic level. Child Work Items record the implementation blockers.

## Verification expectations

- Run bun run check.

subject: Prove pinned local semantic stack
description:
## What to build

Retire native-runtime uncertainty by pinning and probing the approved local embedding and vector-storage stack on the initial supported Bun/platform target.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact compatible versions of node-llama-cpp, @libsql/client, and native libsql dependencies are pinned.
- [ ] The canonical EmbeddingGemma artifact URI, immutable checksum, dimensions, GGUF validity, runtime compatibility, and license obligations are verified.
- [ ] Local-only model resolution, one finite embedding, native vector storage, exact cosine top-K, update/delete, client closure, and database cleanup are proven.
- [ ] Cold-load, one-vector latency, and peak-memory observations are recorded as advisory evidence.
- [ ] Probe code is removed or retained only as an opt-in integration smoke test, and no native or licensing blocker remains.

## Source

Derived from .specs/PLAN-agentic-memory-semantic-index.md: Phase 0 — Compatibility proof and dependency lock.
context:
## Execution context

Time-box this as a feasibility gate. Use the exact approved model URI and establish constants that production implementation can trust rather than guessing from package documentation.

## Relevant project context

- The repository uses Bun workspaces and Effect v4.
- Inspect third-party source under the repository's required vendored-reference paths before using APIs; do not import or edit vendored source.
- Consult .repos/effect/LLMS.md and native Effect patterns for Effect code.
- Normal test and check commands must not download or load the real model.

## Dependency context

None. This gate must complete before product code depends on the native stack.

## Verification expectations

- Run the platform probes explicitly.
- Run bun run check after dependency and retained-test changes.

subject: Provision the shared model during init
description:
## What to build

Make a successful vault initialization guarantee that the approved embedding artifact is available in the shared XDG-compatible Agentic Memory cache, with safe retry and reporting behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A small Effect model service exposes local inspection, explicit installation, and bounded embedding operations with live and fake adapters.
- [ ] Init downloads only an absent artifact, validates GGUF magic and checksum, and never leaves an interrupted artifact looking valid.
- [ ] Failed provisioning does not leave a newly created vault looking initialized; rerunning init on a compatible vault ensures model availability idempotently.
- [ ] Init human and JSON results report model state and preserve one valid JSON document on stdout while progress uses stderr.
- [ ] The canonical and existing-vault .gitignore handling idempotently ignores .agentic-memory/index/ without regressing Git or overwrite behavior.
- [ ] Tests use fake caches and make no network or real-model calls.

## Source

Derived from .specs/PLAN-agentic-memory-semantic-index.md: Phase 1 — Initialization provisions the shared model; Init result contract.
context:
## Execution context

Implement model provisioning as a domain service whose live adapter alone owns node-llama-cpp, XDG cache paths, download policy, validation, and runtime cleanup. Init is the only initial public workflow allowed to download.

## Relevant project context

- Existing init workflow: packages/core/src/vault/VaultTemplate.ts.
- Existing CLI adapter: packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts.
- Init JSON schemas: packages/core/src/cli/CliResults.ts.
- Canonical ignore file: packages/vault-template/template/.gitignore.
- Keep CLI output and core ownership directional and preserve current safe-overwrite behavior.

## Dependency context

Blocked by the pinned-stack proof because production constants and native APIs must be verified first.

## Verification expectations

- Add behavior-focused core and CLI tests with fake model layers.
- Run bun run check.

subject: Index one fixture vault end to end
description:
## What to build

Deliver the first complete public indexing path from a fixture vault's managed Markdown through deterministic chunking and fake embeddings into a real temporary native-vector libSQL database.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Managed-path discovery, normalization, symlink policy, layer classification, content hashing, and basic policy metadata move to one vault-owned interface consumed by deterministic recall and indexing.
- [ ] Pure versioned frontmatter parsing, heading-aware chunking, line provenance, prompt formatting, hashes, and compatibility fingerprints cover the specified edge cases.
- [ ] A deep indexing module exposes inspect, synchronize, and delete contracts while hiding SQL, model paths, vectors, chunk IDs, and fingerprints from CLI callers.
- [ ] The initial index command indexes every managed document, including sources, using local-only inference and a real temporary libSQL adapter with scoped resources.
- [ ] Persisted metadata, documents, chunks, fixed-dimension vectors, per-document transactions, and exact cosine ordering are verified through public repository behavior.
- [ ] The CLI registers index and returns typed human/JSON results without exposing implementation details.
- [ ] Current deterministic recall and its benchmark baseline remain behaviorally unchanged.

## Source

Derived from .specs/PLAN-agentic-memory-semantic-index.md: Phase 2 initial end-to-end slice; Managed documents; Chunking; Module Design; Derivative Data Model.
context:
## Execution context

Build the narrow first tracer bullet that indexes one fixture vault end to end. Introduce only seams that hide genuine model, repository, inventory, or workflow complexity, with pure chunking and fingerprint policy owned once.

## Relevant project context

- Recall-specific inventory currently lives in packages/core/src/recall/RecallDocuments.ts and must move behind a neutral vault-owned interface without changing public recall behavior.
- Core public exports are declared in packages/core/package.json; expose only CLI-needed domain contracts.
- Register the thin command through packages/cli/src/cli.ts and a new packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts.
- Use fake embeddings for normal workflow tests and real libSQL only in scoped temporary integration tests.
- Follow the repository ban on type-only import declarations, any, assertions, and non-null assertions.

## Dependency context

Blocked by init provisioning because it establishes the approved model constants, cache contract, and local-only embedding service.

## Verification expectations

- Add pure, workflow, libSQL integration, CLI, recall-regression, and exact-cosine tests appropriate to this slice.
- Run bun run check.

subject: Complete incremental index lifecycle
description:
## What to build

Complete the semantic index lifecycle so synchronization performs content-hash-correct incremental updates, recovers safely from failures, rejects incompatible state, and explicitly deletes derivative state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An unchanged complete index returns already_current without loading or invoking the model.
- [ ] New files alone are embedded; changed files replace and re-embed all owned chunks atomically; deleted files and chunks are removed without unrelated embeddings.
- [ ] Completion snapshots are written only after the planned run succeeds, failed replacements are not accepted, and later synchronization can finish an incomplete index.
- [ ] Incompatible schema or compatibility fingerprints fail with explicit delete-then-index guidance and never rebuild implicitly.
- [ ] Synchronization and deletion share a vault-specific lock and release model, database, and lock resources through scoped finalizers.
- [ ] index --delete safely removes the database, sidecars, lock state, and derivative directory; returns deleted or already_absent; and preserves Markdown and shared model cache.
- [ ] Typed results, errors, and CLI tests cover all incremental counts and statuses.

## Source

Derived from .specs/PLAN-agentic-memory-semantic-index.md: Phase 2 incremental and deletion cases; Freshness and Incremental Algorithm; Deletion; Error Semantics.
context:
## Execution context

Extend the initial vertical path rather than creating parallel inventory, freshness, or persistence rules. Content hashes determine correctness; modified time may only optimize.

## Relevant project context

- Keep SQL schema and libSQL rows private to the repository adapter.
- Persist complete versus incomplete state explicitly.
- Changed-document vectors must all be produced and validated before the replacement transaction commits.
- Public results must not reveal document paths, chunk text, vectors, scores, prompts, SQL, or provider traces.
- Do not add --rebuild; rebuilding is delete followed by index.

## Dependency context

Blocked by the initial end-to-end fixture path because incremental planning extends its inventory, compatibility, embedding, and repository contracts.

## Verification expectations

- Verify no-op, add, change, delete, failure/retry, incompatibility, lock, and idempotent deletion behavior.
- Run bun run check.

subject: Report semantic readiness through status
description:
## What to build

Expose one read-only readiness calculation through status --vault and a future recall guard while preserving the existing project-link status mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Readiness validates the vault, inspects the local model without download, discovers and hashes managed documents, validates persisted metadata, and computes inventory differences without inference or mutation.
- [ ] Vault status distinguishes ready, missing, stale, incomplete, incompatible, and invalid states with accurate new, changed, deleted, and unchanged counts.
- [ ] Human and Effect Schema-backed JSON output report vault, model, index, recallReady, and actionable warnings without internal implementation details.
- [ ] Completed observational reports return exit code 0 even for not_ready or invalid; execution or encoding failures remain nonzero.
- [ ] status selects vault mode when --vault is supplied and otherwise preserves current --project-root JSON and human behavior.
- [ ] A typed requireCurrentSemanticIndex operation fails before future query embedding whenever readiness is false.
- [ ] Production recall remains on the current deterministic implementation.

## Source

Derived from .specs/PLAN-agentic-memory-semantic-index.md: Phase 3 — Vault status and shared readiness; Readiness inspection; Vault status result.
context:
## Execution context

Make the workflow-owned readiness calculation the only owner of freshness rules. Status and future recall consume it rather than reproducing model, metadata, or inventory checks.

## Relevant project context

- Existing project-link status is packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts with schemas in packages/core/src/cli/CliResults.ts.
- Existing project-root mode must remain compatible.
- Vault inspection must not download, load the model runtime, invoke embeddings, mutate the database, or repair state.
- Return expected readiness conditions as data; preserve typed operational failures at adapter boundaries.

## Dependency context

Blocked by the complete incremental lifecycle because inspection must share its finalized planner, metadata, compatibility, and completion semantics.

## Verification expectations

- Test every readiness fixture, mode selection, exit semantics, guard behavior, and existing project-link compatibility.
- Run bun run check.

subject: Harden semantic index lifecycle
description:
## What to build

Harden the finalized indexing and readiness lifecycle against unsafe paths, malformed derivative state, invalid model output, concurrency, interruption, and native-resource leaks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Coverage proves managed-file symlinks cannot escape the vault and index deletion cannot resolve outside its safe derivative path.
- [ ] Concurrent indexing reports index busy without corrupting state.
- [ ] Corrupt or unsupported databases, malformed metadata, wrong vector dimensions, and non-finite vectors produce precise typed outcomes.
- [ ] Success, failure, interruption, retry, and deletion release model contexts, libSQL clients, files, locks, and temporary artifacts.
- [ ] Interrupted runs preserve only valid per-document transactions and remain not ready until a complete snapshot is written.
- [ ] An opt-in real-model smoke test verifies semantic nearest-neighbor ordering without becoming a normal-CI or network gate.
- [ ] Normal tests remain deterministic and offline.

## Source

Derived from .specs/PLAN-agentic-memory-semantic-index.md: Phase 4 hardening deliverables; Error Semantics; Testing Strategy.
context:
## Execution context

Use adversarial behavior tests to harden the public lifecycle and adapter seams. Fix underlying resource and state semantics rather than suppressing Effect diagnostics or adding CLI-specific workarounds.

## Relevant project context

- File, path, lock, model, and database resources must use scoped acquisition and finalization.
- Keep normal tests independent of the shared real-model cache.
- Retain precise adapter causes and map them to domain errors without calling filesystem, model, or database failures semantic not_found.
- Preserve public result privacy and current deterministic recall.

## Dependency context

Blocked by both the complete incremental lifecycle and shared readiness reporting because hardening covers their finalized success, failure, and interruption paths.

## Verification expectations

- Run targeted adversarial and opt-in smoke checks as applicable.
- Run bun run check.

subject: Publish semantic indexing guidance
description:
## What to build

Publish the finalized local semantic-index operating contract so users can provision, index, inspect, delete, recover, and hand off to future recall work without undocumented knowledge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README quick start covers model provisioning, explicit indexing, readiness status, and deletion from a new vault.
- [ ] Architecture documents derivative per-vault semantic state while preserving Markdown as the source of truth.
- [ ] Schema documentation marks .agentic-memory/index/ as generated, ignored, and outside required committed control-plane memory.
- [ ] CLI help and examples describe init, index, index --delete, and both status modes accurately.
- [ ] Supported platforms, XDG cache resolution, offline behavior, expected model size, progress streams, incompatibility recovery, and safe deletion are documented.
- [ ] The recall handoff names the single readiness operation and internal exact-cosine retrieval seam without exposing model, filesystem, or SQL details.
- [ ] Documentation confirms no vault-version bump is required and generated model/database artifacts stay out of Git status.

## Source

Derived from .specs/PLAN-agentic-memory-semantic-index.md: Phase 4 documentation and release readiness; Completion Criteria.
context:
## Execution context

Document only finalized, verified behavior. The user journey must reach status: ready through explicit commands and explain offline and delete-then-index recovery without implying automatic recall indexing.

## Relevant project context

- Primary docs: README.md, docs/architecture.md, and docs/schema.md.
- CLI package guidance and command examples must match implemented flags and JSON contracts.
- Generated databases and shared models must never be presented as committed memory content.
- Do not claim production recall uses semantic retrieval; this project stops at the readiness and repository handoff.

## Dependency context

Blocked by lifecycle hardening so platform, cleanup, failure, and recovery guidance reflects verified behavior.

## Verification expectations

- Exercise the documented init-to-ready flow where practical.
- Confirm generated artifacts are ignored by Git.
- Run bun run check.
